title: Proper global trace comparison; Varshavsky 1.2.5
statement:
Let $(C,c,u)$ be an admissible correspondence on $(X,K)$, with
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, and let $(f,g):(C,c)\to(D,b)$ be a proper pushforward
diagram of [def-trf-coefficient-pushforward]: $f:X\to Y$ and $g:C\to D$ are
proper and $b_ig=fc_i$ for $i=1,2$. Assume the exceptional admissibility of
[def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps]. Let
$h:F_c=\operatorname{Fix}(c)\to F_b=\operatorname{Fix}(b)$ be the induced
map, proper by [lem-trf-fixed-map-proper]. Then

$$
h_*\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)
=
\operatorname{Tr}_b\bigl([f,g]_!u\bigr)
\qquad\text{in }\operatorname{Hom}(A_{F_b},\omega_{F_b}),
$$

where $\operatorname{Tr}$ is the trace class of [def-trf-trace-class] and
$h_*$ is the Borel–Moore pushforward of [def-trf-borel-moore-pushforward].
No properness over $s$ of $X,Y,C,D$ and no Cartesian leg square is
required.

external.place: Throughout, $Rc_!$ and $Rb_!$ are retained, so the proper-support hypothesis of SGA 5, III, Theorem 4.4 is not imposed.

proof.text: Put $u'=[f,g]_!u$ and $K'=Rf_*K$, using [def-trf-coefficient-pushforward]. By [lem-trf-fixed-map-proper], the maps $h:F_c\to F_b$ and $q=f\times f$ are proper. We may therefore use all the notation of [def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps]: $P_X,P_Y,\rho_f,\delta_K,\delta_{K'},[u]_P,[u']_P,\zeta_c,\zeta_b,\Xi,\mathsf E,\tau_f,\tau_h$. In particular $\Xi:Rb_!Rg_*\cong Rq_*Rc_!$ is natural, and $\zeta_c,\zeta_b$ are isomorphisms. The exceptional admissibility needed in that definition is an explicit hypothesis of this theorem. Only $f,g,q,h$ are identified as proper maps; no leg square is assumed Cartesian. Since $f$ is exceptionally admissible, [def-trf-admissibility] specifies $Rf_!:D^b_{ctf}(X,A)\to D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$. The proper comparison $Rf_*=Rf_!$ specified in [def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps] therefore gives $K\prime\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$, as required for the target trace.

By [prop-trf-trace-class-unconditional], the trace sections of $u$ and $u'$ are defined under the given admissibility and finite-Tor hypotheses, with $K'\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ supplied by Step 1. Write $\alpha_c=\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)$ and $\alpha_b=\operatorname{Tr}_b(u')$. The trace-class definition [def-trf-trace-class] and the final displayed construction of the trace map in the statement of [def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps] identify their ordinary adjoints as
$$
\begin{aligned}
T_c&=\zeta_c^{-1}\circ Rc^!\delta_K\circ\widetilde u_P
=Ri_{c*}\alpha_c\circ\eta_{i_c}:A_C\longrightarrow Ri_{c*}\omega_{F_c},\\
T_b&=\zeta_b^{-1}\circ Rb^!\delta_{K'}\circ\widetilde {u'}_P
=Ri_{b*}\alpha_b\circ\eta_{i_b}:A_D\longrightarrow Ri_{b*}\omega_{F_b}.
\end{aligned}
$$
Here $\widetilde u_P:A_C\to Rc^!P_X$ and $\widetilde {u'}_P:A_D\to Rb^!P_Y$ are the respective source sections followed by the external-duality isomorphisms specified in that definition. For each pair $(a,v)=(c,u)$ or $(b,u')$, the global-sections adjunction of [def-trf-trace-class] sends $\widetilde v$ through the displayed sheaf morphism defining the trace map. The ordinary adjunction $Li_a^*\dashv Ri_{a*}$ of [fix-prop-adjunctions], clause (1), sends a section $\alpha_a$ to $Ri_{a*}\alpha_a\circ\eta_{i_a}$, yielding both formulas. The constructible exceptional adjunctions specified by [def-trf-admissibility] give, by naturality of their counits,
$$
\varepsilon_c\circ Rc_!(\zeta_cT_c)=\delta_K\circ[u]_P,
\qquad
\varepsilon_b\circ Rb_!(\zeta_bT_b)=\delta_{K'}\circ[u']_P,
$$
because $[u]_P=\varepsilon_c\circ Rc_!\widetilde u_P$ and $[u']_P=\varepsilon_b\circ Rb_!\widetilde {u'}_P$ by the kernel-class definition. Only the constructible exceptional adjunction is used.

source.place: Step 1: trace class in adjoint form; replace the point-normalization pointer by the explicit kernel-definition statement

proof.text:
For any $\varphi:A_C\to Rc^!M$, let $\varphi^\flat=\varepsilon_c\circ Rc_!\varphi$. The definition of $\mathsf E$ in [def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps], with the constructible exceptional adjunction specified by [def-trf-admissibility], gives $\varepsilon_b\circ Rb_!\mathsf E=Rq_*\varepsilon_c\circ\Xi$. Thus, by naturality of $\Xi$, the exceptional adjoint of $\mathsf E\circ Rg_*\varphi\circ\eta_g$ is
$$
\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon_b\circ Rb_!\mathsf E\circ Rb_!Rg_*\varphi\circ Rb_!\eta_g
&=Rq_*\varepsilon_c\circ\Xi\circ Rb_!Rg_*\varphi\circ Rb_!\eta_g\\
&=Rq_*\varepsilon_c\circ Rq_*Rc_!\varphi\circ\Xi\circ Rb_!\eta_g\\
&=Rq_*\varphi^\flat\circ\Xi\circ Rb_!\eta_g.
\end{aligned}
$$
For a map $\psi:Rq_*M\to N$, naturality of $\varepsilon_b$ also says that postcomposing this map by $Rb^!\psi$ postcomposes its adjoint by $\psi$. These are substitutions in the defining formulas for adjunction, not an additional exchange theorem.

Apply [lem-trf-trace-source-exchange] to $u$ and then the evaluation identity (1) of [lem-trf-trace-map-exchange]. They have exactly the proper-pushforward and exceptional-admissibility hypotheses in force here and give
$$
\begin{aligned}
\delta_{K'}\circ[u']_P
&=\delta_{K'}\circ\rho_f\circ Rq_*[u]_P\circ\Xi\circ Rb_!\eta_g\\
&=R\Delta_{Y*}\tau_f\circ Rq_*\bigl(\delta_K\circ[u]_P\bigr)\circ\Xi\circ Rb_!\eta_g.
\end{aligned}
$$
The second equality uses only the displayed evaluation identity and functoriality of $Rq_*$ after the first equality. In particular neither equality invokes a Cartesian leg square or properness of the correspondence supports over $s$.

source.place: Step 3: the kernel calculations, first displayed identity

proof.text:
Use Step 3 with $M=R\Delta_{X*}\omega_X$, $\varphi=\zeta_cT_c$, and $\psi=R\Delta_{Y*}\tau_f$. Steps 2 and 4 show that $\zeta_bT_b$ and
$Rb^!(R\Delta_{Y*}\tau_f)\circ\mathsf E\circ Rg_*(\zeta_cT_c)\circ\eta_g$
have equal exceptional adjoints. The constructible exceptional adjunction bijection specified by [def-trf-admissibility] therefore makes these two maps equal. Now apply the support identity (2) of [lem-trf-trace-map-exchange] and factor $Rg_*(\zeta_cT_c)$ by functoriality. This gives
$$
\zeta_bT_b=\zeta_b\circ Ri_{b*}\tau_h\circ Rg_*T_c\circ\eta_g.
$$
The source identification in that support identity is precisely $Rg_*Ri_{c*}=Ri_{b*}Rh_*$, using $gi_c=i_bh$. Since $\zeta_b$ is an isomorphism by [def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps], postcomposing by its inverse yields
$$T_b=Ri_{b*}\tau_h\circ Rg_*T_c\circ\eta_g.$$
No faithfulness of $Ri_{b*}$ is used in this cancellation.

source.place: Step 3: equality of exceptional adjoints and support comparison

proof.text:
By [def-trf-coefficient-pushforward], $gi_c=i_bh$. Apply the ordinary composite-unit formula in [fix-prop-adjunctions], clause (3), at the constant coefficient objects (so each relevant pullback sends the constant object to the constant object). In its adjunction-compatible composition identifications it reads
$$
Rg_*\eta_{i_c}\circ\eta_g
=\eta_{gi_c}=\eta_{i_bh}
=Ri_{b*}\eta_h\circ\eta_{i_b}.
$$
Substitute $T_c=Ri_{c*}\alpha_c\circ\eta_{i_c}$ into Step 5, and use the same direct-image composition identification $Rg_*Ri_{c*}=Ri_{b*}Rh_*$. Functoriality followed by the displayed unit equality gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
T_b
&=Ri_{b*}\tau_h\circ Rg_*Ri_{c*}\alpha_c\circ Rg_*\eta_{i_c}\circ\eta_g\\
&=Ri_{b*}\bigl(\tau_h\circ Rh_*\alpha_c\circ\eta_h\bigr)\circ\eta_{i_b}.
\end{aligned}
$$
This is direct substitution in the cited unit formula; it does not require a separate exceptional composition theorem on any enlarged coefficient category.

source.place: Step 4: the unit identities and substitution

proof.text:
Step 2 also gives $T_b=Ri_{b*}\alpha_b\circ\eta_{i_b}$. The ordinary adjunction bijection of [fix-prop-adjunctions], clause (1), sends a section $\beta:A_{F_b}\to\omega_{F_b}$ to $Ri_{b*}\beta\circ\eta_{i_b}$; applying its inverse to the equality in Step 6 proves
$$
\operatorname{Tr}_b([f,g]_!u)=\alpha_b
=\tau_h\circ Rh_*\alpha_c\circ\eta_h.
$$
The definition of $\tau_h$ in [def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps] is exactly the last two arrows in [def-trf-borel-moore-pushforward]: $Rh_*\omega_{F_c}\cong Rh_!Rh^!\omega_{F_b}\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_h}\omega_{F_b}$. Hence the right-hand side is $h_*\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)$, proving the stated equality. The argument retains $Rc_!$ and $Rb_!$ throughout.

source.place: Step 4: final ordinary adjunction and Borel–Moore pushforward

proof_origin.place: Steps 1–4, with adjunction substitutions expanded and citation scope repaired; checked against Varshavsky 1.2.2, 1.2.5, 4.3.4 and 4.4

split_report.summary: Preserved the full finite-coefficient statement and the unit kernel/exchange route. Reused the existing properness, kernel-source and kernel-map exchange nodes. Replaced the point-only normalization citation and the existence-only trace-map citation by the explicit trace formula in the statement of the kernel-pushforward definition. Expanded the elementary mate and ordinary-unit calculations; removed the unnecessary exceptional-composition citation. No new nodes or attachment. Second reading: cite the constructible exceptional adjunction definition rather than the ambient-admissibility clause of fix-prop-adjunctions; expose finite-Tor preservation for K prime and both trace-adjoint calculations.
split_report.blueprint: Current main-20261015 theorem proof: setup and Steps 1–4 are realized by proof steps 1–7. Unit sk-p-proper: properness by lem-trf-fixed-map-proper; notation/evaluation by def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps; kernel comparisons by lem-trf-trace-source-exchange and lem-trf-trace-map-exchange; support by lem-trf-trace-map-exchange; final unit/adjunction assembly by this node.

tool_uses.why: Ordinary Hom bijections and ordinary composite-unit normalization are generic tools for the final adjunction calculation; no node of sk-p-proper states these general laws. Exceptional adjunctions instead come from the constructible datum in def-trf-admissibility.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-ND-478f0eef1 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all seven steps in full. The statement is unchanged and matches the current main-20261015 blueprint theorem and Varshavsky Prop. 1.2.5 (p. 10; 1.1.6 case (ii), 1.2.2): f and g are proper, F is ctf, c and b need not be proper, and the legs are swapped consistently to the blueprint convention. No target is weakened. There are no new nodes, leaves or attachments; the only change outside the item is the unit's realized/realized_by fields. Step 1: K' is in D^b_ctf because def-trf-admissibility makes Rf_! preserve ctf and Rf_*=Rf_!. Step 2: T_c comes from the explicit t_{c,K} formula at the end of the kernel-pushforward definition; its exceptional adjoint delta_K[u]_P follows from the kernel-class definition and counit naturality. Every object is ctf, so the constructible adjunction of def-trf-admissibility is the right one. The second reader correctly replaced fix-prop-adjunctions clause (2), which assumes the strong ambient FullCD admissibility. Step 3: the three mate equalities hold (definition of E, naturality of Xi, definition of phi-flat). Step 4: source-exchange plus map-exchange clause (1), exactly as stated. Step 5: equal exceptional adjoints, map-exchange clause (2) with Rg_*Ri_c*=Ri_b*Rh_*, then cancellation of the isomorphism zeta_b; no Cartesian leg is used. Steps 6-7: the composite-unit formula (clause 3), the inverse of the clause (1) bijection, and tau_h matching the last two arrows of the Borel-Moore pushforward. proof_deps equals the union of uses. Removing prop-trf-pairing-point-normalization (Spec k only) and the existence-only lem-trf-trace-map-from-external-duality was correct (C4). The citation of prop-trf-trace-class-unconditional is genuine (existence of Tr_b(u')) and keeps the unit route reaching sk-p-pairing. Accepted tool_use: fix-prop-adjunctions, ordinary clauses (1) and (3) only. lem-trf-proper-pushforward-trace-class is a remark that uses this theorem, not a duplicate. Edge cases: identity maps, u=0, empty F_c, and the two-point fold map (u'=u1+u2, both sides equal tr u1 + tr u2) all check out. For maintenance only, not a fault here: def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps does not list def-trf-admissibility in its stmt_deps. No fixes.
